subject: Customer showcase prep: live-loop scripting & audience Q&A plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Customer showcase prep: live-loop scripting & audience Q&A plan

Team —

ByteWave has confirmed a 20-min customer showcase slot (30-min room). Asking us to provide: a one-sheet (2-sided PDF) for the customer case, a short demo script that fits 8–10 minutes of live loop time, and a separate 5-minute audience Q&A cue sheet. Goal: make the customer look great while highlighting Redwood's predictable latency and cost controls on hybrid deployment.

Can we do the following by Monday EOD?
- Ben: draft one-sheet content (3 key outcomes, metrics, quote + short architecture callout) — attach PPT or doc
- Marissa: create two demo loop scripts (fast-start + degraded-mode fallback) with expected token counts and fallback messaging for customer narrator
- Vanessa: coordinate with ByteWave on AV & stage map; confirm mic options and in-room latency expectations

I attached an initial outline (showcase_talking-points_v1.docx) and a plain-text customer TL;DR for voiceover (customer-TL-dr.txt). Also added a suggested live-loop snippet doc (script_snippets_v2.md) — these are rough.

Key success criteria: clean one-sheet for handout, demo loops that can run from hosted and Dedicated (note which model variant to call out), and a Q&A cheat sheet that outfits the customer with 3 soundbites and 2 fallback responses.

Thanks — LMK if timing is tight.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer showcase prep: live-loop scripting & audience Q&A plan

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> ByteWave has confirmed a 20-min customer showcase slot...

Thanks Rachel — attaching the first pass as requested. Outline included in "showcase_one-sheet_ben_v1.pptx" (I exported two slides + notes). High-level:
- Top-line metric: 3x reduction in median token cost for steady-state queries on customer workload (benchmarks attached)
- Architecture callout: Dedicated pool + KV prefix caching to hit sub-100ms p95 on short-turn queries
- Customer quote placeholder: asked PM to approve by Monday

Questions for Marissa: for degraded fallback loop, do we want a scripted line that explicitly calls out "auto-fallback to 8-bit quantized variant" or keep it higher level? My recommendation: keep it non-technical on the handout, technical detail in the demo notes.

Attachments: showcase_one-sheet_ben_v1.pptx (slide export), benchmark-summary.csv (stub).

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Hill <samantha@bytewaveevents.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer showcase prep: live-loop scripting & audience Q&A plan

Hi team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Confirming ByteWave will provide a single podium mic + lav, a 1/8" line for laptop audio, and a confidence monitor. I've attached the stage map (bytewave_stage_map.pdf) and our AV constraints (AV_constraints_ByteWave.pdf).

A few notes from the production side:
- Recommended live-loop timing: 8–9 minutes demo, 3–4 minutes customer narrative/promo, 4–5 minutes audience Q&A.
- For in-room latency testing, we'll run an end-to-end check 30 minutes before showtime; bring a secondary laptop to run the Dedicated fallback test in case of network issues.
- We can provide a short backstage run-through with the customer 20 minutes before doors open (10 min hands-on + 10 min mic/test).

If you want us to host the confidence monitor feed, send the streaming URL to prod@bytewaveevents.com 48 hours before the event.

—Samantha
Samantha Hill
Producer, ByteWave Events
Samantha.Hill@bytewaveevents.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer showcase prep: live-loop scripting & audience Q&A plan

Thanks — review notes below and I've updated the shared drive doc (see link).

Quick slide/script review:
- One-sheet: move the architecture blurb to the back and replace with 3 customer outcomes on the front; shorten metric line to a single percent + 1 sentence explanation.
- Fast-start demo: open with an "Expectations" slide (10s) that sets up latency/cost tradeoff so audience knows what to watch for.
- Degraded-mode fallback: write the script as an "operator action" (e.g., "Switch to Dedicated-fallback profile; announce short handling time") — avoid product-lingo like quantization in front of the customer.
- Q&A cheat sheet: add 2 soundbites for the customer to use if asked about data residency and one-line fallback ("we can run in your VPC or a dedicated pool with audit logging").

I'll consolidate Ben's PPT and my script snippets into a 1-page handout (PDF) and upload to the Drive. Vanessa — can you confirm mic test & run-through time with Samantha and add it to the calendar invite?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Field Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
